stemMd: Ethene reacts with bromine by addition across its double bond. What happens to the carbon–carbon bond?

options.label: C
options.textMd: It remains double while each carbon exceeds its normal valence.

options.label: E
options.textMd: It becomes a single bond as one bromine bonds to each carbon.

explanationMd: The pi component of the double bond is replaced by two carbon–bromine bonds. The carbon–carbon sigma bond remains, producing a saturated dibromo compound.

distractorRationale.b: Addition reduces the multiple bond order.
distractorRationale.c: The pi bond is consumed to maintain normal valence.
distractorRationale.d: No nitrogen-containing peptide linkage is formed.
